id: title:danielcarletti:don t repartition finer on oom history when partitions are tiny

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a guard in the warehouse ingestion worker to skip unnecessary repartitioning when the largest partition is well under budget, even if OOM history exists, preventing potential infinite loops or skipped-event behavior while retaining observability. Includes regression tests.
review.reason: Adds a constant and a conditional guard to skip repartitioning when the largest partition is far under budget, even if OOM history exists. Updates tests to cover this behavior. This is a substantive, bounded correctness and reliability improvement.
review.uncertainty: The exact production impact and the specific warehouse connector this guards are not fully established by the provided hunk descriptions, though the mechanism is clear.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No score assigned; tier requires assessment of implementation and checks.

observations.behavior: Adds a constant OOM_WORKING_SET_AMPLIFICATION and a guard to skip repartitioning when the largest partition is far under budget, even if OOM history exists.
observations.code_quote: if not over_budget and max_bytes * OOM_WORKING_SET_AMPLIFICATION < budget:
observations.posthog_connection: Prevents unnecessary, potentially infinite, finer-grained repartitioning and skipped-event loops when OOM history is a false positive, while still recording the max partition size for observability.

observations.behavior: Updates a test to use a smaller budget value, and adds a new test asserting that tiny partitions do not trigger repartitioning despite OOM history.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression and behavior tests for the new guard, including a specific test for the false-positive OOM scenario described in comments.
